input.quote: 10.5 DISCLAIMER OF WARRANTIES. EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY REPRESENTATIONS OR GRANTS ANY WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, EITHER IN FACT OR BY OPERATION OF LAW, BY STATUTE OR OTHERWISE, AND EACH PARTY SPECIFICALLY DISCLAIMS ANY OTHER WARRANTIES
input.rationale: Harpoon (counterparty) gives a substantial express warranty package in Section 10.2 (title to and validity/enforceability of the Existing Patents, non-infringement of Third Party rights, right to grant the licenses, no breach of the Harpoon In-License Agreements, accuracy and completeness of Regulatory Documentation and Know-How, no false statements to FDA, no debarment), and these are backed by performance-standard covenants: Section 3.8.4 requires all Development activities, including the Initial Development Activities, to be performed "in good scientific manner and in compliance with all Applicable Law", and Section 10.3.3 requires Harpoon to employ Persons with appropriate knowledge, expertise and experience — the collaboration-agreement equivalent of the playbook's professional/workmanlike and compliance-with-laws warranties. Critically, the Section 10.5 disclaimer is expressly carved back for "THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN", so it does not swallow those warranties and this is nowhere near the "AS IS" walk-away position. Remedies are real and appropriate to the deal type: AbbVie's material-breach notice and step-in/cost-recovery mechanics under Sections 3.1.2 and 3.6, indemnification under Section 11.2, and termination rights (including immediate termination on debarment under Section 10.2.14). The rule's fixed conformance window (12 months software / 90 days services) with repair-replace-refund is inapplicable to a drug development and option collaboration, where no software or services deliverables are supplied; that absence is noted rather than flagged. No redline proposed.
